title: Westgate Community Clinic: bids, budget and the agreement
scenario:
**Westgate Health**, a nonprofit, is building a **24,000 sf community clinic**. The project is design-bid-build. The architect's agreement is based on B101-2017 (terms summarized in the Agreement Summary resource).

- The architect's 95% CD estimate matched the budget. The CDs were submitted to the owner on **March 1**, and bids were opened on **March 28**.
- The lowest bona fide bid exceeds the owner's budget for the cost of the work. The regional construction cost index rose about **1%** between the estimate and the bid opening, in line with the cost consultant's forecast.
- A donor funded the **rooftop photovoltaic array**. The clinic's board wants to keep it if at all possible.
- The board has decided to accept bid alternates and, if needed, revise scope to stay within the budget. It won't increase the budget.
- The board treasurer has suggested withholding the architect's procurement-phase fee "until the budget problem is solved."

resources.title: Agreement Summary
resources.body:
### Owner–architect agreement (B101-2017 basis): key terms as filled in
| Term | Agreed |
|---|---|
| Basic compensation | 8% of the cost of the work |
| Phase allocation | SD 15% · DD 20% · CD 40% · Procurement 5% · Construction 20% |
| Owner's budget for the cost of the work | $9,600,000 (approved at end of CDs) |
| Additional services | Hourly, at the architect's billing rates (project architect $150) |
| Construction-phase limits | 2 site visits per month; 1 review and 1 resubmittal per submittal |
| Time limit | Services to be completed within 30 months of the agreement date |
| Dispute resolution | Mediation, then arbitration |

Other provisions follow the standard B101-2017 terms. Summary written for this case study; it isn't AIA text.

resources.title: Bid Results and Cost Summary
resources.body:
### Bid results (lowest bona fide bid)
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Base bid | $10,050,000 |
| Alternate 1: delete entry canopy | −$95,000 |
| Alternate 2: delete casework upgrade | −$140,000 |
| Alternate 3: delete rooftop PV array | −$310,000 |
| Alternate 4: reduce site paving and lighting | −$260,000 |

### Cost summary
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Owner's budget for the cost of the work | $9,600,000 |
| Architect's 95% CD estimate | $9,550,000 |

questions.stem:
Refer to the scenario and the Bid Results and Cost Summary.

The board asks the architect which alternates to accept so the contract sum is within the budget, keeping as much scope as possible while respecting the board's wish about the photovoltaic array.

Which alternates should the architect recommend?

options.explanation: These deduct exactly the $450,000 gap, but they remove the donor-funded PV array the board wants to keep.
These deduct $400,000, leaving the bid $50,000 over budget.
Correct. They deduct $495,000, bringing the bid to $9,555,000 while keeping the PV array.
These deduct $355,000, leaving the bid $95,000 over budget.

questions.stem:
Refer to the scenario and the Agreement Summary.

After accepting the alternates, the board decides to revise the scope further so it has a small construction contingency within the budget, and it asks the architect to modify the construction documents. The board asks how the modifications will be compensated.

How should the architect be compensated for modifying the documents?

options.text: As an additional service, because the bids exceeded the budget
options.explanation: Bids over budget alone don't make redesign an additional service.
Correct. Bidding began within 90 days, and the 1% rise was foreseeable, so the redesign is part of the architect's obligation.

options.text: Only after the budget is adjusted for escalation
options.explanation: The 90-day escalation adjustment doesn't apply, because bids were opened 27 days after CDs.

options.text: Through a deduction from the contractor's fee
options.explanation: The contractor isn't a party to the owner–architect agreement.

questions.explanation:
1. Bids opened 27 days after CDs → no 90-day escalation adjustment (§6.4)
2. The 1% market change was forecast, not unforeseeable → §6.7 redesign without additional compensation

questions.stem:
Refer to the Agreement Summary and the Bid Results and Cost Summary.

The architect performed design, documentation and bidding services for all four alternates. The board accepts Alternates 1, 2 and 4, so that work won't be built. The treasurer asks whether the architect is owed anything for the deleted alternates.

How much compensation is the architect owed for its services on the deleted work?

options.text: $0, since the work won't be built
options.explanation: Under a percentage fee, deleted portions are paid to the extent services were performed.
This covers SD, DD and CD only. The architect also performed procurement services on the alternates.
Correct. 8% × $495,000 × 80% (SD + DD + CD + procurement) = $31,680.
This includes construction-phase services that won't be performed.

questions.confidenceNote: Deleted-portion compensation per B101-2017 §11.6; confirm in your copy.

questions.stem:
Refer to the Agreement Summary.

During construction, the owner asks the architect to visit the site every week during the three months of framing and rough-in, about 13 visits in all. Each visit takes the project architect 5 hours, including travel and a field report. The owner asks what this will cost beyond the basic fee.

What additional fee should the architect propose?

options.explanation: This prices only 6 visits, the number included in basic services.
Correct. 13 − 6 included = 7 extra visits × 5 hours × $150 = $5,250.
This prices all 13 visits, including the 6 in basic services.
This prices 4 extra visits, as if 9 visits were included.

questions.explanation:
1. Included = 2 per month × 3 months = 6 visits
2. Extra = 13 − 6 = 7 visits
3. Fee = 7 × 5 hours × $150 = $5,250

questions.stem:
Refer to the scenario and the Agreement Summary.

The architect's invoice for procurement-phase services is due. The treasurer still wants to withhold it until the budget problem is solved, even though the architect has agreed to modify the documents. The architect wants to protect the relationship and its fee.

How should the architect respond?

options.text: Accept the withholding until the redesign is complete
options.explanation: The agreement doesn't permit withholding fees as a penalty for bids over budget.

options.text: Explain the agreement's terms and propose mediation
options.explanation: Correct. The redesign is the architect's remedy, withholding as a penalty isn't permitted, and the agreement makes mediation the first step.

options.text: File a demand for arbitration right away
options.explanation: Mediation comes first under the agreement.

options.text: Stop work on the redesign without notice
options.explanation: Suspension requires written notice, and stopping now would harm the owner's schedule.

questions.explanation: B101: no withholding as a penalty (§11.10.3). Redesign is the architect's remedy. Disputes go to mediation first.
